title: The Spot Price Is What Silver Costs — The Premium Is What You Actually Pay

segments.text: The spot price is what silver costs. The premium is what you actually pay. Knowing the difference determines how much silver you get for your money.

segments.narration: Junk silver — pre-1965 US coins — carries the lowest premiums in the market, typically three to eight percent. There's no fabrication cost, just melt value plus a dealer margin. It's the best value for pure silver exposure.
American Silver Eagles carry an 18 to 28 percent premium above spot. You get US Mint quality, legal tender status, and high liquidity anywhere in the country — but you pay for that reputation.

Buying generic rounds or junk silver instead of Eagles saves roughly 15 percent in premium costs. Over a long accumulation period, that difference means meaningfully more silver for the same dollars spent.
